about: What docs/adr/0014's rule promises for the stream server's cases on a real player, checked by scripts/stream-cases. Each case plays `path` on the stream server (or `url`, where {dead} is a port nothing listens on) for `seconds`, and expects one of two outcomes. `plays`: no terminal error, and no silence after the first audio longer than `maxGapSeconds`, and with `network`, audio again within `resumesWithinSeconds` of JS hearing the device online after the last step that turns the network on. `error`: the terminal error `atSeconds` from play, give or take `toleranceSeconds`. A limit given per platform is an object keyed by platform. `network` turns the device offline and online at seconds from play; such a case needs a device whose network the script controls. `platforms` limits a case to some platforms; the default is all.

cases.name: a stream that closes after 10 s of audio plays on
a stream that closes after 4 s of audio plays most of the time and gives up 120 s after its load
a stream that closes after 2 s of audio gives up 120 s into its silence
a connection that sends its burst and then nothing gives up at 120 s of silence
a connection that stops sending after 10 s of audio, on every connection, plays on
a dead address gives up 12 s after its first failure
a stream offline for 40 s plays again once the network returns
